title: Tug of war was an Olympic sport
hook: For 20 years, Olympic medals went to teams pulling on a rope.
peek: Tug of war was part of the Olympics from 1900 to 1920, and some of its strongest teams were policemen. The City of London Police won gold twice, and in 1908 British police teams took every medal.
lede: The playground game was once a serious Olympic event. Tug of war appeared at every Summer Games from 1900 to 1920, with teams, usually of eight, pulling a rope until one side dragged the other over a line. Many of the best teams came from police forces, which had big, fit men and plenty of time to train together.

bullets.text: At the London Games in 1908, the City of London Police won gold, Liverpool Police took silver and a team from the Metropolitan Police won bronze. British police swept the podium.
The American team in 1908 objected to the heavy boots worn by the Liverpool officers, saying they gave an unfair grip. The protest was rejected, and the Americans withdrew.
At Stockholm in 1912, a Swedish police team beat the City of London Police. The London officers won gold again at Antwerp in 1920, the last time the event was held.
The sport left the Olympics as the programme was trimmed, but it never went away. It has its own international federation, world championships and a place at the World Games.
